A Fruitcake-Spiced Canna-Cocktail Without the Booze

Black tea, cranberry and berry preserves with orange peel and warm spice: an alcohol-free holiday glass with a measured THC tincture shaken in.

Key takeaways

  • Chilled black tea, cranberry juice and cherry or blueberry preserves bring fruitcake's dark-fruit depth.
  • Read the tincture label, start low, and shake the dose in before the ice so it mixes through.
  • It's alcohol-free by design; top it with berry seltzer for a sparkling version.
  • Mix the same base without tincture so every guest gets a festive glass.
In this article
  1. Start with the label
  2. The fruitcake flavors
  3. Shake, strain, serve your holiday THC mocktail
  4. Batching and labeling
  5. A zero-THC glass for everyone else
  6. Recipe
  7. Frequently asked questions

This holiday THC mocktail earns its fruitcake name. It starts as a black tea mocktail, with cranberry juice and berry preserves for dark-fruit depth. Orange peel and a pinch of warm spice add the bakery notes, and a measured THC tincture is shaken right in. There's no liquor, just a festive glass that tastes like the holidays.

Start with the label

The dose comes from the tincture, so read its label first: it lists THC in mg per ml. Measure with the marked dropper or a small oral syringe, and start low. Health Canada suggests new consumers begin at 2.5 mg of THC or less. Shake the tincture with the tea, juice and preserves before any ice goes in, so it mixes through the whole drink. Then give it at least 2 hours before a second glass.

The fruitcake flavors

Fruitcake means candied peel, dark fruit and warm spice, so the glass leans on the same notes:

  • Black tea, regular or decaf, for a malty backbone
  • Cranberry juice for tart fruit
  • Cherry or blueberry preserves for jammy sweetness
  • Orange peel and a pinch of cinnamon, allspice or nutmeg
  • Dried or maraschino cherries to garnish

Shake, strain, serve your holiday THC mocktail

Shake everything with the tincture until the preserves dissolve, add ice and shake again, then strain over fresh ice. Twist the orange peel over the glass and drop it in with the cherries. For a sparkling version, strain into a tall glass and top with berry seltzer.

Batching and labeling

Mix to order when you can, so each glass gets its own measured dose. If you batch a pitcher, stir the total tincture dose in thoroughly, label the pitcher 'contains THC' with the dose per cup, and serve it with a measuring cup. Pour out whatever remains once the party winds down instead of saving it, and keep tinctures away from children and pets. If someone drinks an infused glass by accident, call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222.

A zero-THC glass for everyone else

Make the same base without tincture in a second, clearly marked pitcher, so every guest gets the fruitcake glass. Keep the infused version for adults 21+ who know what's in it, and make sure nobody who drinks it drives.

Recipe

Makes
1 drink
Prep time
10 minutes

Ingredients

  • 4 ounces strong black tea, regular or decaf, brewed and chilled
  • 2 ounces cranberry juice
  • 1 tablespoon cherry or blueberry preserves
  • 1 wide strip of orange peel
  • 1 small pinch of cinnamon, allspice or nutmeg
  • THC tincture, measured for 1 serving (see the dosing note)
  • Ice
  • 2 dried or maraschino cherries
  • Optional: 2 to 3 ounces berry seltzer

Steps

  1. Combine the tea, cranberry juice, preserves, spice and measured tincture in a cocktail shaker or a jar with a tight lid.
  2. Shake hard for about 10 seconds, until the preserves have dissolved.
  3. Add a handful of ice and shake for another 10 seconds.
  4. Strain into a rocks glass over fresh ice. Twist the orange peel over the drink, then drop it in with the cherries.
  5. For a sparkling version, strain into a tall glass of ice instead and top with berry seltzer.

Dosing note

One glass, one measured dose: ml of tincture × the label's mg per ml = THC in the drink. Example: 1 ml of a tincture labeled 3 mg per ml is about 3 mg. A homemade tincture is an estimate that depends on the flower's potency and on decarboxylation and extraction losses. Start low, wait at least 2 hours before a second, label any batched pitcher, and keep infused drinks away from children and pets.

Frequently asked questions

How much tincture goes in one mocktail?

Enough for the dose you chose, measured in milliliters. Multiply the ml you add by the label's mg per ml: 1 ml of a tincture labeled 3 mg per ml is about 3 mg, for example. Keep the first glass small, and wait at least 2 hours before deciding on another.

Can I use decaf tea?

Yes. Decaf black tea keeps the same malty backbone with only a trace of caffeine, which makes the glass easier to enjoy late in the evening. Brew it strong, since ice and juice dilute it, and chill it completely before mixing. Rooibos works too, for a naturally caffeine-free glass with a warm, slightly sweet flavor.

Does caffeine change how THC feels?

It might, and there's no reliable way to predict how it will for you. Caffeine is a stimulant, and THC affects people differently, so the pairing can feel different from one person to the next. To keep things simple, brew decaf, so the THC you measured is the one new variable in your glass.

Sources

  1. Health Canada: What you need to know if you choose to consume cannabis canada.ca
  2. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention: Cannabis frequently asked questions cdc.gov
21+
